projects.title: TraceLayer
projects.subtitle: Evidence-centered resume verification with stage-level evaluation
description: A multi-stage system that converts resume claims into an auditable evidence map while preserving uncertainty, identity checks, and source-level provenance.
projects.role: Designed and built the end-to-end verification workflow, deterministic identity gates, evidence promotion rules, runtime evaluation, and report pipeline.
projects.problem: Resume-screening systems can turn self-reported claims into polished summaries without showing whether the underlying evidence is relevant, attributable, or sufficient.
approach: Decompose resumes into atomic claims with stable source anchors and explicit group membership.
Resolve candidate identity before public sources can enter the trusted evidence set.
Separate retrieval from evidence promotion so topical or wrong-person sources cannot influence verification.
Orchestrate the workflow as observable stages while keeping identity, budgets, and failure routing deterministic.
evaluation: Test claim extraction, identity resolution, GitHub ownership, evidence linking, verification states, and end-to-end behavior independently.
Treat wrong-identity approvals and unsupported verified claims as hard-gate failures rather than average-quality tradeoffs.
Track search budgets, connector calls, latency, evidence coverage, and explicit abstention states.
outcomes: Changed the architecture from output-first automation to promotion-only evidence flow with auditable failure states.
Created fixture-backed requirements for wrong-person blocking, unsupported-claim handling, and bounded search behavior.

projects.title: Market Brief Agents
projects.subtitle: Evidence-grounded market research-to-video pipeline
description: A local-first AI system that turns market events into reviewable short-form briefings using retrieval, agent orchestration, validation gates, and deterministic fallbacks.
projects.role: Designed and implemented the local-first workflow, typed contracts, validation boundaries, operator dashboard, and deterministic public demo path.
projects.problem: Market brief generation can look convincing even when sources, claims, scripts, and rendered output drift apart across a long multi-agent workflow.
approach: Review source material before retrieval and preserve provenance in audit bundles.
Use typed manifests to connect research, evidence, script generation, and video rendering.
Expose workflow state through a Streamlit operations view and a Next.js shell.
Render validated scripts through Remotion rather than handing unstructured text directly to video generation.
evaluation: Apply validation gates at research, evidence, script, and render boundaries.
Keep synthetic fixtures and deterministic fallbacks so the public workflow can be exercised without paid APIs or live financial data.
Preserve audit artifacts so each generated claim can be traced to its reviewed inputs.
outcomes: Produced a runnable reference architecture spanning orchestration, retrieval, operator review, and deterministic rendering.
Made failure states inspectable instead of hiding them behind a completed video artifact.

projects.title: Hate Meme Detection
projects.subtitle: Reproducible multimodal BERT, ViT, fusion, and Gemini experiments
description: A reproducible experiment package for comparing text-only, image-only, multimodal fusion, and prompted-model baselines on hate meme detection.
projects.role: Refactored disconnected experiments into a shared package with reusable data loading, configuration, training, evaluation, and prompting interfaces.
projects.problem: Multimodal baselines are difficult to compare when each experiment uses different preprocessing, training loops, metrics, and access assumptions.
approach: Implement text-only BERT, image-only Vision Transformer, ViT+BERT fusion, and Gemini prompting baselines behind consistent workflows.
Share dataset handling, configuration, training loops, metrics, and prompt templates across experiments.
Separate private dataset requirements from public smoke-test fixtures and provider-free checks.
evaluation: Compare unimodal, fusion, and prompted-model approaches through a common evaluation interface.
Use smoke tests that exercise package boundaries without private datasets or external model calls.
Keep experiment configuration explicit so results can be reproduced and reviewed.
outcomes: Turned research scripts into a maintainable experiment package with consistent baselines.
Made the public repository runnable for structural validation without exposing private data.

projects.title: Semantic Resume Screening / TalentAI
projects.subtitle: Resume parsing and semantic candidate matching modules
description: Standalone modules for resume parsing, skill extraction, candidate summarization, and hybrid semantic job matching with API and command-line interfaces.
projects.role: Built the standalone AI modules for parsing, semantic retrieval, skill matching, and title-aware ranking.
outcomes: Combined embedding similarity with skill and title alignment in reusable API and CLI workflows.

projects.title: Semantic Search Benchmarking
projects.subtitle: LSA, LDA, GloVe, and SBERT retrieval comparison
description: Benchmarking workflows comparing classical topic models and dense transformer embeddings on MS MARCO-style retrieval tasks.
projects.role: Implemented comparable retrieval and evaluation workflows across sparse, topic-model, and dense approaches.
outcomes: Measured precision, recall, F1, average precision, and MAP through a shared benchmark workflow.

projects.title: CEBERT
projects.subtitle: Causal regularization for robust hate speech detection
description: Official implementation of the AACL-IJCNLP 2022 paper using causal strength and entropy regularization to reduce spurious lexical correlations.
projects.role: Co-developed the causal formulation, regularized training objective, and adversarial evaluation.
outcomes: Reached 85.9% and 86.0% accuracy on word-replaced and misspelled test sets, outperforming the strongest reported baselines.

projects.title: MDL-MLM
projects.subtitle: Minimum description length analysis for adversarial NLP
description: Official repository for the Entropy 2024 article using masked language modeling and description length to detect adversarial manipulation.
projects.role: Developed data preparation, masked-language-model, perturbation, and description-length analysis workflows.
outcomes: Established an information-theoretic signal for detecting adversarially altered tokens without access to the original text.
